refuters.argument:
Not refuted. Clause-by-clause, `Bridge.B3`/`Bridge.B3_unsorted` are neither stronger nor weaker in content than printed Lemma B3 (BRIDGE.md:495, excerpt line 3).

HYPOTHESES (printed: "the three parameter-difference sign changes in SM type T, together with its central conditions"). SM type T (sm-1-polygons.tex:735-738) = Z_pt = ∅, Z_c = {{e,f,g}}, and on each of the three edges the difference of the two crossing parameters of the other two edges changes sign at 0 (def:germ 670-671: ∃δ>0, φ(P(t))φ(P(−t))<0 for 0<t<δ). Lean `SM.WallGerm.TripleAt e f k` (NamedWallPredicates.lean:30-34) is exactly: `g.pointZeros = ∅ ∧ g.concurrences = {{e,f,k}} ∧ g.SignChanges (edgeParameter P e f − edgeParameter P e k) ∧ g.SignChanges (edgeParameter P f e − edgeParameter P f k) ∧ g.SignChanges (edgeParameter P k e − edgeParameter P k f)`. `pointZeros`/`concurrences` = `pointZeroTriples`/`concurrenceTriples` of the centre (GermDefinition.lean:12-14; ZeroTriples.lean: card 3, pairwise `remote`, a common point of the three `edgeInterior`s) = Z_pt, Z_c verbatim (`pointZeros_empty_iff : pointZeros = ∅ ↔ G1 center`). `edgeParameter P i j = cramerFirst (P i) (P j) (edge P i) (edge P j) = det(P j − P i, edge P j)/det(edge P i, edge P j)` (Chambers.lean:86, ContinuousGeometry.lean:18) is the parameter along edge i (equals CV's t_j along e_i by `crossParam_eq_edgeParameter`, Setup.lean:572), so the three differences are measured on E_e, E_f, E_k — the base edges SM names — and on a type-T germ all three pairs cross at every time (`crosses_const`, B2), so the total Cramer formula agrees with SM's crossing parameter wherever SM's condition reads it. `WallGerm` (WallGerm.lean:13-19: continuous curve on Ioo(−r,r), `SM.Generic = G1 ∧ G2` off 0, not generic at 0) is def:germ verbatim. `g.SignChanges` (GermSignChange.lean:10-12) is def:germ's product test plus a harmless `δ ≤ radius` (`signChanges_iff_local`). Nothing SM imposes is dropped; nothing beyond `3 ≤ n`/`[NeZero n]` (SM's standing n ≥ 3) is added. The extra `rep e < rep f < rep k` in `B3` is §0's naming convention ("choose e<f<g in those representatives") and is removed in `B3_unsorted`, so no type-T germ is excluded.

CONCLUSION (printed: "CV transversality for the zero set (3)"). `Event.Transversal := ∀ m ∈ E.zeroSet, E.SignChanges m.eval` (Events.lean:589); `zeroSet = {m | m.eval E.center = 0 ∧ ∃ t : E.Parameter, t.val ≠ 0 ∧ m.Relevant (E.curve t)}` (561-562) is def:event's Z verbatim (d1_setup.tex:1076-1079), ranging over the full indexed `CV.Member` family with CV's index side conditions (Setup.lean:638-643) and `Active`/`Relevant` (674-683). So the Lean asserts sign changes ONLY for members of the event's zero set (which B2 identifies with (3)) — no claim about members outside Z. `eventOfTriple` has `radius := g.radius`, `curve := g.curve` (B1.lean:126-134), so `Event.SignChanges` (Events.lean:570-572) and `g.SignChanges` are the same formula on the same data and `signChanges_eventOfTriple_iff` is `Iff.rfl`. CV's d1_setup.tex does not define "changes sign at t=0" independently (line 1086 is its only use); BRIDGE.md B3 itself equates "SM's exact sign-change definition" with "exactly CV transversality" (excerpt lines 105, 143) and notes that for continuous members nonzero on the punctured half-intervals the product test coincides with constant opposite signs on the two halves — which holds here since activation is constant along the germ (B2). So the sign-change notion is not a weaker reading of CV/BRIDGE.

I could construct no type-T germ covered by the printed lemma but excluded by the Lean, and no configuration on which the Lean claims a sign change (or any property) that the printed lemma does not. Non-blocking notes only: (a) `B3` carries the §0 ordering hypotheses, discharged by `B3_unsorted`; (b) `edgeParameter` is a total Cramer formula rather than a partial "crossing parameter", but agrees with it at every time of a type-T germ; (c) the CV "changes sign" notion is rendered by SM's germ product formula, as BRIDGE.md B3 itself does.
